title: Gradual routemap for model deprecation: signal harmonization, migration kits, and archiving cadence
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We need a repeatable, low-friction workflow for phasing out older model versions while minimizing customer disruption and preserving SLAs. Current ad-hoc retirements have caused unexpected client regressions and increased support load.

Goals:
- Provide a deterministic multi-stage deprecation routemap that maps model lifecycle state to required actions (notice, opt-in pin, migration kit, archival).
- Publish machine-readable performance profiles and explicit migration suggestions so customers can automatically pin, test, and roll forward.
- Instrument telemetry signals to detect active usages, breaking changes, and migration friction.
- Reduce live-customer rollback incidents for deprecations by 75% within first 6 months.

Scope: Covers hosted API product model variants and curated open-model entries in the catalog (not private on-prem customer-managed weights). Excludes complete model weight purge policies which are handled by infra/ops in a separate runbook.

Deliverables:
- Customer-facing deprecation timeline and templated notices (email + Console banner + API warning header).
- Migration kits: sample pin configs, model-equivalent suggestions, performance delta table, and migration test prompts.
- Internal orchestration checklist for release engineering and support.
- Telemetry dashboard with active pin counts, failing-eval regression rate, and N-day usage decay metric.
acceptance_criteria: Customer-facing deprecation notice template available in Confluence and Console messaging library
Migration kit artifacts (pin example, migration prompts, perf delta CSV) published in model-catalog/docs for all targeted variants
Telemetry dashboard (dash link below) shows baseline active usage, and alerts trigger when 7-day active usage > threshold
Automated warning header included in API responses for pinned Customers for at least 30 days prior to hard-sunset
Runbook entry for final archival steps created and reviewed by Infra and Legal
Pilot deprecation executed for one low-usage model with <10 support incidents and post-sunset compatibility feedback logged

telemetry_signals: active_pin_count: count of customers with explicit pin to deprecated version (daily)
n_day_usage_decay: rolling 7/14/30 day active user delta for model variant
regression_rate_on_eval_suite: percent of eval prompts with degraded output quality compared to recommended replacement
support_tickets_tagged: % change in support tickets mentioning 'regression' or 'model behavior' during deprecation window
failed_integrations: counts of SDK/webhook errors tied to model endpoint changes
notification_templates: Console banner (short): 'Notice: redwood-alpha-2023 will enter planned sunset on 2025-04-15. Pin to a replacement or test migration kits in Console > Models.'
Email subject: 'Action required: Planned retirement of redwood-alpha-2023 — migration guidance inside'

Support canned reply: 'We're winding down redwood-alpha-2023. Please use the migration kit (link) to test redwood-alpha-2024; if you need pinning assistance, reply and we can create a migration window.'
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Pilot, 2025-03-28 to 2025-04-01): Execute deprecation process on low-usage variant; validate telemetry and support load
Phase 1 (Notice, 2025-04-02 to 2025-04-16): Send notices, enable Console banners, publish migration kits and perf profiles
Phase 2 (Encourage Migration, 2025-04-17 to 2025-05-15): Offer assisted pinning windows, SDK warnings, targeted outreach to top pin holders
Phase 3 (Hard Sunset, 2025-05-16): Disable serving on deprecated variant in non-dedicated regions; retain read-only perf profiles and archive telemetry
Phase 4 (Archive, 2025-06-01): Final archival of artifacts and metadata (weights handled separately by Infra); update model-catalog status to 'archived'
risks: Customers rely on subtle behavior of old weights not captured by perf deltas — mitigation: expand eval prompt set and offer dedicated migration windows
High-touch enterprise customers require custom rollback windows — mitigation: Sales and Solutions to offer contract-based extended pinning
Telemetry gaps cause missed active users — mitigation: cross-validate usage with billing records and support tags
API consumer automation may break on header warnings — mitigation: introduce opt-out header and provide SDK upgrade path
open_questions: What is the minimum notice period for enterprise customers under existing contracts? (Legal to confirm)
Should we enable automatic pin-suggestions in Console for customers with regression_rate > 10%?
Do we want to surface migration cost delta (estimated token cost) in the migration kit?
Is there appetite to offer an automated compatibility shim that maps old call shapes to new model responses?
